$comment: Where somebody who does not have Bingd is sent, per platform.
This file exists so that the *shared* link never has to change. What a person
pastes into a group chat is https://bingd.app/i/<token> and it is permanent:
it survives development, Preview, TestFlight, a Play closed test, an open
test, and both public stores. Only the destination behind it moves, and it
moves here — one file, no app rebuild, no reissued invitations.
That is also why no TestFlight or Play URL appears anywhere in app/ or src/.
A temporary distribution URL compiled into the client is a URL that outlives
its own build.
NOTHING HERE IS A SECRET. These are public install pages.
null means 'not available yet', and the page says exactly that rather than
guessing. A store button that 404s is worse than an honest empty state: the
person concludes Bingd does not exist, and the inviter never finds out.
$modeComment: Which Bingd this site is describing: 'beta' or 'public'.
IT IS A PRE-FLIGHT GATE AND NOT A COPY SWITCH, and that changed on 2026-09-10.
There used to be an `isPublic` derived from it that about a dozen strings and the
robots directive branched on. Every one of those is gone: availability is a
per-platform fact that the URLs below already carry, and indexing is per route.
So `mode` changes NO BYTE of the built site. What it still does is refuse to
build 'public' while either storeUrl is null, while the Terms names an
unconfirmed entity, or while TERMS_STATUS in build.mjs is still 'draft'.
IT IS 'beta' TODAY AND THE REASON IS THE THIRD GATE, NOT THE STORES. Both store
URLs are set: iOS since 2026-09-10, Android with this tranche. TERMS_STATUS is
'draft', so a build that flipped this would refuse outright — which is correct,
because 'final' is a record that a lawyer read the document and not a word
written to make a build pass. See L-1 in the public-launch risk register.
So public users already get the public stores while this still says 'beta'. The
flag describes the launch checklist, not the destinations.
Anything unset, misspelt or missing reads as 'beta'. The failure modes are not
symmetric — a stale label costs nothing while no copy reads it, and a premature
'public' would lift noindex on nothing and ship a Terms that calls itself a draft.

$comment: The public TestFlight link, of the form https://testflight.apple.com/join/XXXXXXXX.
Public rather than an email allowlist, deliberately: friend-of-friend is the
whole shape of this beta, and an allowlist means the founder is asked to add
an address every time somebody forwards a link — which is the moment the
invitation stops working. Set this once the build is approved for external
testing; the App Store URL replaces it at public release.
storeUrl SET 2026-09-10. bingd. 1.0 has been on the public App Store since
2026-09-08 (iTunes lookup: trackName 'bingd.', bundleId app.bingd), and this
field was still null — which is why bingd.app offered no install button at all
and read as a dead end. destinationFor() prefers storeUrl over betaUrl, so the
site now sends everybody to the listing. App Review updates that same listing
when a new version is approved, so the URL does not move again.
betaUrl is kept rather than removed: it is the destination again if the listing
is ever pulled, and it costs nothing while storeUrl wins.
storeUrl SET with the public Android tranche. vc12 cleared founder QA and was
submitted to the Google Play production track for a US public launch, so the
canonical Android destination is the ordinary listing:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.bingd
THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE PLAY URL IS WRITTEN. destinationFor() prefers
storeUrl over optInUrl over betaUrl, so setting this field alone moves every
public Android CTA on the site — the front page, the invitation page, the
title page and the profile page — with no second edit and no app rebuild. The
button label and the availability line under it are derived from the same
field, so none of them can disagree with it.
optInUrl is KEPT rather than deleted, for the reason ios.betaUrl is kept: it
is the record of how the closed test was reached, and it is the destination
again if the listing is ever pulled. It never wins while storeUrl is set, and
router.test.mjs asserts that. Tester eligibility and any Google Group
membership are administered in Play Console and deliberately not modelled
here: Bingd does not run a tester list.
betaUrl stays null. It was the slot for a plain listing reachable only after
an opt-in, and a public listing is what storeUrl now holds.
The custom scheme used by the page's 'I already have Bingd' button, and by
nothing else. It is never shared and never shown as a URL.
It has to exist, and the reason is an iOS rule rather than a preference: a
link to bingd.app clicked ON bingd.app is a same-domain navigation, and iOS
deliberately does not hand those to the app. So the one button that has to
work immediately after an install — 'I have it, open it' — cannot be an
https link to this same site. A custom scheme is the only thing that opens
an installed app from its own web page.
`bingd` is the production variant (app.config.ts). The App Store, TestFlight
and every Play track distribute the production variant, so this is the scheme
every installed app will have. A development or Preview build installed by hand
registers bingd-dev / bingd-preview instead and will not answer this button —
which is a founder-device case, not a tester one.
